mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k per month for five consecutive months in the context of an unemployment rate below 4% indicates an overheating labor market, which amplifies wage inflation and cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200000 for 5 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for six consecutive months, regardless of monetary policy stance, signals a broad-based supply contraction that reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.
